gloss: To live; to reside.
To linger (on); to remain fixated.
To be in a given state.
To abide; to remain; to continue.

Any member of a race of beings from (especially Scandinavian and other Germanic) folklore, usually depicted as having some sort of supernatural powers and being skilled in crafting and metalworking, often as short with long beards, and sometimes as clashing with elves.
A person of short stature, often one whose limbs are disproportionately small in relation to the body as compared with typical adults, usually as the result of a genetic condition.
An animal, plant or other thing much smaller than the usual of its sort.
A dwarf star.
Miniature.
To render (much) smaller, turn into a dwarf (version).
To make appear (much) smaller, puny, tiny; to be much larger than.
To make appear insignificant.
To become (much) smaller.
The condition of being a dwarf (person of short stature).
The quality of being puny or inferior.
To decrease, shrink, diminish, reduce in size or intensity.
To fall away in quality; degenerate, sink.
To lessen; to bring low.
To break up or disperse.
A house or place in which a person lives; a habitation, a home.
A planetary (world-like) body of the Solar system, that directly orbits the Sun like the classical planets but does not gravitationally dominate other bodies in the region of its orbit.
declining; growing less
A faint galaxy, devoid of gas, having a higher than normal proportion of dark matter; especially those that orbit the Milky Way and Andromeda
A "sport" in which contestants compete to throw a small person the farthest.
Any galaxy, considerably smaller than the Milky Way, that has only several billions of stars.

A star that is located in the main sequence in the Hertzsprung-Russell diagram, though generally excluding the small minority which fall in the blue band due to their large size and high luminosity; fuses hydrogen into helium in its core.
A tinamou, Taoniscus nanus, also known as the least tinamou.
A small European herbaceous perennial elder, species Sambucus ebulus.
One who discovers by building on previous discoveries.
